projects.name: Modular Desk Lamp
projects.thesis: Explore a repairable light platform that can shift between task, ambient, and video-call modes in compact workspaces.
projects.role: Fictional demonstration authored for the industrial-design-portfolio Skill

evidence.claim: A modular desk light could support multiple compact-workspace routines.
Screen glare may affect preferred light placement.
Video calls may require a second lighting position.
Limited desk depth may constrain the base footprint.
One movable light head may serve task, ambient, and call modes.
Clamp, weighted-base, and rail routes represent distinct architectures.
The weighted-base route is the provisional selected direction.
Cylindrical joints and a replaceable sleeve express modularity.
The concept separates the light head, arm, power module, and base.
Reach, tipping, joint effort, and glare are planned prototype variables.
A wider base and shorter lower arm are proposed stability responses.
evidence.source: Illustrative iteration, not a tested result

evidence.claim: The final visualization represents a concept resolution only.
Ergonomics, optics, thermal behavior, cost, and repair remain unresolved.

assumptions.statement: Compact-workspace users need one light to support several modes.
Modular replacement would be valuable enough to justify separable components.
